subject: Post-call: Merchantly inference TCO levers & budget alignment
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@merchantly.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 21:03:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: Merchantly inference TCO levers & budget alignment

Hi Sara — great to meet earlier. Thanks for walking through Merchantly's fraud-prevention use case and the high-level volumes. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we stay aligned on scope and budget: 

Pain points you confirmed
- Model latency spikes impacting fraud-check throughput at peak (5–7PM PST).
- Cost unpredictability: token-heavy prompts across enrichment + history lookups.
- Need for deterministic response SLAs for rejection decisions.

Goals you shared
- Keep tail latency below 150ms for decisioning path.
- Target monthly inference spend around $25k–$30k for Q1 pilot.
- Proof of >2x ROI on reduced fraud losses within 3 months.

Cost/TCO levers we discussed (how Redwood helps)
- Batching + workload-aware pooling: improves throughput during bursts while meeting latency SLOs.
- Prefix/KV caching for repetitive enrichments to cut per-request tokens by up to ~40% on sample workloads.
- Model sizing & quantization: recommend a quantized Llama-2 13B variant for the decision path to balance latency and cost.
- Smart routing: route non-critical classification (bulk scoring) to cheaper capacity regionally.

Prelim pilot proposal (short)
- Duration: 8 weeks (2-week integration, 4-week pilot, 2-week analysis).
- Scope: Decision path (real-time), and batch re-score job for historical analysis.
- Minimal test load: 100k requests/day peak, average prompt length ~220 tokens (input+output).
- Expected unit economics: with caching + batching we estimate 35–50% reduction vs naive per-request baseline.

Asks / next steps (please):
1) Confirm monthly average and peak requests for the decisioning endpoint (range is fine).
2) Share an anonymized sample prompt (or length histogram) so we can finalize token estimates.
3) Confirm budget target for Q1 pilot and procurement timing.
4) If okay, I will share a short pilot SOW + a preliminary TCO workbook (attached) for you and your procurement team.

Attachments: merchantly_prelim_tco.xlsx (simple estimator + two pilot scenarios).

I'll plan to follow up with a proposed SOW and a 30/60/90 pilot ROI slide once we get the numbers above. Available windows for a kickoff: Thu 14–16 PST or next Tue 10–12 PST.

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0122

From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@merchantly.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Cc: Merchantly Procurement <procurement@merchantly.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: Merchantly inference TCO levers & budget alignment

Thanks, Rachel — helpful recap and much appreciated. Confirmation items below: 

Numbers / constraints
- Avg requests/day (decisioning): 60k/day; peak windows ~120k/day.
- Typical prompt length: input ~180 tokens, expected output ~50 tokens (total ~230 tokens).
- Q1 pilot budget: Procurement has ~ $25,000 reserved for this pilot; additional spend will need exec approval.
- Procurement timeline: We can sign a short pilot SOW within 3 weeks; standard vendor review + SOC2 checklist will take ~2–3 weeks concurrently.

We attached a short doc listing required security controls and a sample data flow diagram. Our security team will likely want to see KV caching controls and whether we can limit retention windows for cached keys.

We are OK to proceed with the SOW and the TCO workbook you mentioned. Two asks from our side:
1) Please provide an example configuration showing the batching policy + estimated latency impact for 120k/day peak.
2) Confirm whether Redwood can limit prefix/KV cache retention to 24h for pilot mode (security requirement).

I'll loop in procurement once you share the SOW. Available for kickoff: Thu next week 14–15 PST.

Attaching: merchantly_requirements.pdf

Sara Liu
Head of ML Ops, Merchantly
sara.liu@merchantly.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 18:00:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: Merchantly inference TCO levers & budget alignment

Nice recap, Rachel — good thread. Quick internal note with proposed next moves and estimates so we can act quickly once Sara confirms: 

Internal action items
- Dev: please prepare a pilot config with the following baseline: quantized 13B model, batching target 64, dynamic batching window 8ms, KV cache TTL configurable (default 24h for pilot). Estimate expected p95 latency at ~120–140ms for decision path at 120k/day with burst traffic patterns. (Dev, can you validate with our simulator?)
- Sales: I will prepare a 2-page SOW and a one-slide ROI summary for execs showing 35–50% cost savings vs baseline and projected fraud-reduction ROI. Target to send SOW to Sara by EOD Fri.
- Security: flag KV cache TTL and retention controls for the SOC2 checklist; we should propose encryption-at-rest + customer-managed KMS for pilot.

Notes on budget posture
- If Merchantly can commit to the $25k pilot, we can cover initial integration hours within a standard pilot credit bucket; that keeps procurement friction low. Larger commitments can move to Dedicated capacity discounts.

I'll draft the SOW and attach the preliminary TCO sheet you prepared. Rachel — please confirm you'll request the anonymized sample prompt from Sara and confirm the kickoff slot Thu 14–15 PST.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
